# KIT-189 results (proposed wording, VAL-41: the owner edits)

Outcome **O1** (`outcome.md`). Recommended default: Benjamini-Hochberg over the whole size-filtered family; the q-value offered with its measured failure stated (VAL-86). Numbers from `results/` (score run 45311934798).

## 1. Trade-off text of each option (text T, generated by `score-k189.R`, `results/options.tsv`)

**Default: Benjamini-Hochberg over the whole size-filtered family.** Assumption: Benjamini-Hochberg over every term of 10 to 500 proteins; its guarantee needs independent or positively dependent tests, which overlapping Gene Ontology sets do not ensure. On random protein lists (no true signal; 18 settings: E. coli full proteome and a 2,000-protein subset, yeast; lists of 25, 126 and 400 proteins; with and without parent terms), 1.0 % to 2.5 % of lists had at least one significant term (highest one-sided 95 % upper limit 3.1 %; line 7.5 %): it controlled false calls in 18 of 18 settings, failed in 0 and was not determined in 0. Lists with 10 or more significant terms: at most 0.1 % (E. coli 2,000-protein subset, lists of 25, parent terms). On lists of 126 with one planted process, mean false discovery proportion 0.1 % to 1.7 % (highest upper limit 2.7 %; controlled in 18 of 18 settings, failed in 0, not determined in 0), the planted term called in 74.8 % to 100.0 % of lists where it was tested.

**Offered: The q-value (as shipped).** Assumption: Storey's estimate of the share of true nulls assumes null p-values uniform on (0, 1); the route adjusts only the terms with at least one list protein, which breaks that assumption for small sets. On random protein lists (no true signal; 18 settings: E. coli full proteome and a 2,000-protein subset, yeast; lists of 25, 126 and 400 proteins; with and without parent terms), 1.7 % to 42.9 % of lists had at least one significant term (highest one-sided 95 % upper limit 44.8 %; line 7.5 %): it controlled false calls in 10 of 18 settings, failed in 6 (E. coli full proteome, lists of 25, no parent terms: lower limit 15.1 %; E. coli full proteome, lists of 25, parent terms: lower limit 19.9 %; E. coli full proteome, lists of 126, no parent terms: lower limit 13.3 %; E. coli 2,000-protein subset, lists of 25, parent terms: lower limit 14.0 %; yeast, lists of 25, no parent terms: lower limit 8.0 %; yeast, lists of 126, no parent terms: lower limit 39.2 %) and was not determined in 2. Lists with 10 or more significant terms: at most 23.6 % (yeast, lists of 126, no parent terms). On lists of 126 with one planted process, mean false discovery proportion 0.2 % to 35.7 % (highest upper limit 38.7 %; controlled in 15 of 18 settings, failed in 3 (E. coli full proteome, small planted process, lists of 126, no parent terms: lower limit 7.5 %; yeast, small planted process, lists of 126, no parent terms: lower limit 29.5 %; yeast, mid planted process, lists of 126, no parent terms: lower limit 18.2 %), not determined in 0), the planted term called in 80.5 % to 100.0 % of lists where it was tested, and against Benjamini-Hochberg over the same terms it called the planted term at most 3.8 % more often (paired; highest one-sided lower limit over 18 settings 0.0 %; a material gain needs 5.0 %).

**Not named by O1, for the owner (VAL-86 offers "Benjamini-Hochberg"): Benjamini-Hochberg over the terms with at least one list protein.** Assumption: Benjamini-Hochberg over the terms with at least one list protein; that family is selected on the p-value (p below 1), for which Benjamini-Hochberg has no general guarantee. On random protein lists (no true signal; 18 settings: E. coli full proteome and a 2,000-protein subset, yeast; lists of 25, 126 and 400 proteins; with and without parent terms), 1.6 % to 8.2 % of lists had at least one significant term (highest one-sided 95 % upper limit 9.3 %; line 7.5 %): it controlled false calls in 16 of 18 settings, failed in 0 and was not determined in 2. Lists with 10 or more significant terms: at most 0.5 % (E. coli full proteome, lists of 25, parent terms). On lists of 126 with one planted process, mean false discovery proportion 0.2 % to 2.6 % (highest upper limit 3.8 %; controlled in 18 of 18 settings, failed in 0, not determined in 0), the planted term called in 78.5 % to 100.0 % of lists where it was tested.

## 2. Methods sentence for the recommended default (after its product ticket)

"For organisms outside g:Profiler's set, a Gene Ontology term was called significant when its Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value, computed over every term with 10 to 500 proteins of the background (terms without a list protein entering with p = 1), was below 0.05. In simulations through this route (random and planted lists of 25, 126 and 400 proteins drawn from the reviewed UniProt proteomes of E. coli K-12, a 2,000-protein subset of it, and S. cerevisiae, the last run through this route as a stand-in; with and without parent terms; 2,000 random lists per setting), 1.0 % to 2.5 % of random lists had any significant term, and on lists of 126 with one planted process the mean false discovery proportion was at most 1.7 %. Storey's q-value as clusterProfiler computes it, over the terms with at least one list protein only, is offered as an option; on random lists of 25 and 126 proteins it exceeded 7.5 % in 6 of 18 settings (Bonferroni-adjusted lower limits above 7.5 %), with up to 42.9 % of random lists having any significant term and 23.6 % ten or more (yeast, lists of 126, no parent terms)."

## 3. Methods sentence for the shipped flag, as measured (for records made before the change)

"A term was called significant when its Storey q-value, computed by clusterProfiler (enrichit 0.2.0) over the terms with at least one list protein, was below 0.05. Because terms without a list protein are left out before the adjustment, the estimated share of true null terms falls far below 1 on many random lists; on simulated random lists the share of lists with any significant term was 1.7 % to 42.9 % depending on the proteome, list size and parent terms (failing a 7.5 % line in 6 of 18 settings, two of them with parent terms, both with lists of 25 proteins), against 1.6 % to 8.2 % for Benjamini-Hochberg over the same terms."

## 4. Corrected sentence for KIT-173 `results.md` section 4

Replace "Storey's q-value assumes nearly independent tests; on 20 random lists from the E. coli proteome 1 list in each setting had any significant term (95 % interval 0.1 % to 25 %), and without parent terms one random list had 120 terms significant by q-value and none by Benjamini-Hochberg." with:

"Storey's q-value, computed over the terms with at least one list protein, does not hold its nominal rate on this route (KIT-189): on 2,000 random lists of 126 annotated proteins from the E. coli proteome, 16.0 % (95 % interval 14.4 % to 17.6 %) had any term significant by q-value without parent terms and 5.8 % (4.8 % to 6.9 %) with them, against 3.8 % and 2.6 % by Benjamini-Hochberg over the same terms and 1.6 % and 1.7 % by Benjamini-Hochberg over every term of 10 to 500 proteins; KIT-173's random list of 126 entries (draw 5, reproduced in KIT-189's check E0) had 120 terms significant by q-value and none by Benjamini-Hochberg."

## 5. Computed after scoring, reported (not part of the declared text T; the owner edits, VAL-41, VAL-86)

Implementation audit `AUDIT-KIT-189-impl-20261124.md`, I05. No new run: every figure below is recomputed from the committed rows (`rows/*.tsv.gz`) or read from the committed score tables. Paired figures: per replicate of a planted cell where the planted term was tested, `planted_called` of one arm minus the other (columns `planted_tested`, `planted_called`), mean and t interval, recomputed locally with standard-library Python; false discovery proportion: `calls_null / calls` per list (0 without a call), mean and t interval, same recomputation; BH above 5 %: `results/classifications.tsv` (estimate, `lowerB`). These are post-hoc comparisons, outside the declared template and the declared classifications. The option texts in section 1 and `results/options.tsv` column `text` stay as declared until the owner answers.

- **The q-value**, appended: "Against the default (Benjamini-Hochberg over the whole size-filtered family) it called the planted term up to 5.8 points more often with parent terms (E. coli 2,000-protein subset, small process: 23 more of 400 lists, none fewer) and up to 8.8 points more often without (yeast, large process), a gain that comes with the failures above. On planted lists of 25 with parent terms (E. coli, mid-size process; reported, not deciding) its mean false discovery proportion was 10.7 % (95 % interval 8.5 % to 12.9 %)."
  How obtained: cell 15 with parent terms, 23 of 400 tested lists Q called and BHf did not, 0 the reverse (0.0575; 95 % 0.035 to 0.080); cell 22 without parent terms, 12 of 137 (0.0876); cell 13 with parent terms, mean FDP 0.1067 (95 % 0.085 to 0.129) over 200 lists.
- **Benjamini-Hochberg over the whole size-filtered family**, appended: "Against the q-value as shipped it called the planted term up to 5.8 points less often with parent terms and up to 8.8 points less often without, and against Benjamini-Hochberg over the terms with at least one list protein up to 3.8 and 5.1 points less often; never more often."
  How obtained: the same pairs; BH minus BHf in cell 15 with parent terms 15 of 400 (0.0375; 95 % 0.019 to 0.056), cell 22 without 7 of 137 (0.0511); over all 18 deciding planted cells no list on which BHf called the planted term and Q or BH did not.
- **Benjamini-Hochberg over the terms with at least one list protein**, appended if it is offered (the owner's question): "In 2 of the 18 random-list settings (lists of 25 without parent terms: E. coli full proteome 7.2 %, yeast 8.2 %) it exceeded its nominal 5 % (lower limits 5.4 % and 6.3 % after Bonferroni adjustment over the 108 classifications; observed after scoring, not a declared classification)."
  How obtained: `results/classifications.tsv` cells 1 and 7 without parent terms, arm BH: estimates 0.0720 and 0.0825, `lowerB` 0.0543 and 0.0635.
